AbbVie’s Analytics and Performance Excellence (APEX) function is seeking a highly strategic, analytical, and collaborative Associate Director to provide analytics leadership for the Business Evolution Strategic Development (BESD) Team. This role will drive impactful business analytics and insights to help AbbVie anticipate and navigate evolving healthcare environments, especially focusing on market access and policy disruptors. The Associate Director will bridge Market Access and Patient Services (MAPS) Team within APEX and BESD (Business Evolution Strategic Development) team objectives by leading modelling, advanced insights and analytics supporting forward-looking strategies, enabling enterprise readiness, and shaping market access policies and outcomes for AbbVie’s diverse U.S. portfolio. This role requires a strong grasp of healthcare policy, payer analytics, and strategy formulation within a collaborative, cross-functional environment. Key Responsibilities: Lead the planning and execution of analytics to inform market access strategies, price reform and policy analysis, with actionable recommendations for AbbVie leadership. Identify payer opportunities/threats through deep dive analytics ('Follow the Dollar', claims analysis, and scenario modeling). Foster positive relationships and close collaboration with teams including Government Affairs, Finance, Legal, Corporate Affairs, Brand, and Market Access. Communicate complex findings and insight-driven narratives to senior leadership and cross-functional teams, enabling improved payer knowledge and strategic decision-making. Monitor external environment and translate emerging trends (political, regulatory, legislative, commercial) into strategic recommendations for AbbVie’s business evolution. Advise on analytics infrastructure enhancements to drive business impact. Skills Action and Accountability: Own responsibility for activities within relevant workstreams, and engage and inspire cross functional stakeholders to advance towards clear objectives and strategies; make quick, but informed decisions, as appropriate, to ensure best paths forward in the midst of change market and policy dynamics. Constantly engage, guide, and support cross-functional team to address roadblocks, challenges, resourcing constraints and other dynamics. Leadership and Influence: Influence and persuade across multiple external and internal stakeholders. Collaboration and Teamwork: Work effectively with internal stakeholders, external market experts and partners. Bachelor’s degree required; master’s degree (MBA or related business/science) preferred. 10+ years of progressive analytical/ insights experience in healthcare industry (pharma, consulting, government affairs, market access, public policy, etc.). 1-2 years pharmaceutical market access experience with deep understanding of Health Plans, PBMs, Hospitals, Specialty Pharmacies, and healthcare policy stakeholders. Strong insurance channel experience and understanding (i.e. Medicare, Commercial etc.) Strong business acumen, strategic and analytical thinking, and executive presence. Exceptional communication and influencing skills, with the ability to distill complex information into compelling, concise messages. Strong organizational skills, flexibility, attention to detail, and experience in collaborative, dynamic environments. Exceptional communications and executive presence, critical thinking and interpersonal skills, strong ability to influence without authority, the ability to speak and write persuasively and with clarity, strong organizational skills, flexibility, and adaptability to changing requirements, resourcefulness and creativity, strong attention to detail, a proven track record of being able to work drive towards deadlines and an ability to work collaboratively in a fluid organizational and external environment. Must be an individual who works well in a team environment and enjoys working in a collegial, collaborative and fun, yet highly demanding culture Preferred: Experience in policy shaping, price reform strategy, and enterprise-level stakeholder partnership. Proficiency with pharmaceutical data sources (formulary, claims).

Proactively seeks out strategic business opportunities with high-level business unit executives. Proven experience with Agile methodologies, and Scrum or Kanban frameworks. Proven experience collaborating with engineering and design teams spread across the globe. 3+ years’ experience as a people leader/manager. Strong analytical skills with the ability to draw insights that drive the business forward. Determines and develops approach and solutions to problems. Fluent in English as AbbVie’s designated global business language. Preferred: Strong understanding of Salesforce Health Cloud. Work experience in the pharmaceutical industry. Experience working with data analytics.

Position Purpose: Responsible for effective maintenance of drum inventory and proper preparation of burn plans for containerized waste in order to incinerate in accordance with all regulatory requirements. Creates K-mixes, tank blends and direct feed records for incineration of bulk wastes. Maintains files associated with burn plans. Accumulates waste tracking information from throughout the facility. Performs QA/QC on paperwork and reconciles discrepancies prior to entering data into Access Inventory/Waste Tracking System. Primary Duties/Responsibilities: Receives, assimilates, and reviews for accuracy and completeness all waste tracking paperwork and records (bulk receipts, drum receipts, material transfers, materials fed to facilities, and site generated waste) associated with waste processed through the facility and/or released for disposal at other sites. Inputs data into Access inventory system. Updates information in Access computer system after discrepancy resolution. Identifies and locates missing data for compliance with state and federal regulations. Submits information to Environmental Department for the EPA required one year PCB exception report. Assimilates all PCB manifests along with appropriate continuation sheets, and container building transfer logs and resolves any discrepancies. Inputs PCB data into Access Inventory System, including container unique ID numbers and out-of-service dates. Prepares and distributes Certificates of Destruction and communicates with customers and CWM Billing Department as required. Burn Plan Preparation: Receives reviewed/signed paperwork to be placed in Burn Plan Packages. Enters review date, analytical and profile information on each profile. Minimizes the number of Burn Plans by combining multiple line items and receiving ticket numbers. Prepares burn plan folders (staging, stage to conveyor, conveyor to kiln). Notifies other departments of available burn plans and distributes plans daily. Once Container Burn Plans are completed, they are distributed with Kmix and Tank Blends to Shift Supervisor. This position is responsible to create k-mixes, burn plans, and tank blends for incineration, including data entry to create the finished k-mix, burn plan or tank blend. This position also assists in entry of profile and Access data as appropriate. Frequent use of AS400 profile system is required. This position collects the completed disposal tickets and distributes the necessary K-mix and paperwork to operations, waste tracking, billing, and process planning as required. This position has a high requirement for both speed and accuracy of data entry. The preparation of mixes, burn plans and blends must provide for a continuous supply of waste to operations. Participates in monthly physical inventory reconciliation, preparing inventory worksheets, entering inventory locations, and reconciling inaccurate inventory information. Prepares monthly report of total inventory volume (in pounds) for accounting. Make cover sheets listing all Burn Plans, K-mixes and tank farm feedlots. List any extreme conditions or burn priorities on the Burn Plan cover sheets. This position is “on-call” during evenings, weekends and holidays to provide 24 hour plant service as needed, on a weekly rotating basis. Establish and maintain files and records pertaining to Certificates of Destruction and original transfer logs. Performs special projects as assigned by the Waste Blending Supervisor or other designated staff. Minimum of one weekend workday per month is required for physical inventory. Other duties as assigned. Education/Experience/Background: High School or GED equivalent required. One year verifiable computer data entry and clerical experience as a primary job function including Microsoft Access or similar, IBM AS400 data entry, Microsoft Windows. 1 year hazardous waste experience. Knowledge/Skills/Abilities: Computer proficiency in Microsoft Office Suites and Lotus Notes Good written and verbal communication skills Strong team player Excellent interpersonal skills Strong customer orientation

AI.Accelerate Overview: Are you a technically curious and ambitious undergraduate student with a passion for Artificial Intelligence? ServiceNow invites you to explore our AI.Accelerate program where you can develop practical AI skills and gain hands-on experience in a dynamic, fast-paced, and immersive environment. This eight-week unpaid bootcamp is designed to provide a comprehensive introduction to the core concepts and techniques of AI, with a focus on practical application and real-world problem-solving. You'll learn from experienced instructors, work on challenging projects, and collaborate with a cohort of talented peers. Dates: June 15 – July 31, 2026 (Virtual) + Week 8—beginning of August (In Person) Location: Virtually via Zoom Duration: 4 hours a week (plus homework) What You'll Learn: Agentic AI Foundations: Understand what makes an AI system "agentic" — including autonomy, reasoning, and action-taking — and how LLMs are evolving from chat tools into decision-making agents. Agentic Design Patterns: Explore key architectural patterns including React, chain-of-thought, tool use, and memory, and understand the difference between single-agent and multi-agent systems and when to use each. Prompt Engineering: Learn techniques for writing reliable, production-grade prompts that drive consistent and predictable agent behavior at scale. Building Agents: Design agents that use tools, APIs, and external data sources, and learn how to structure agent memory — both short-term and long-term — for complex, multi-step tasks. Multi-Agent Orchestration: Build and manage multi-agent workflows where agents collaborate, delegate, and hand off tasks to accomplish goals that no single agent could complete alone. Evaluation Frameworks: Learn why evaluations are the most critical part of building AI systems and how to design frameworks that define what to measure and how to measure it effectively. AI Safety & Responsible Use: Understand real-world failure modes including hallucination, prompt injection, and behavioral drift, and learn how to build guardrails and safety checks into agentic pipelines. Capstone Project: Design, build, evaluate, and defend an AI agent from scratch — putting every concept from the program into practice and presenting your work to a panel of ServiceNow engineers and leaders. Innovative Learning Structure: A blend of lectures, hands-on laboratories, and collaborative projects fostering a cohort- based, hands on learning experience. The program concludes with an in-person experience where participants showcase their capstone project, explore career opportunities at ServiceNow, and connect with the broader engineering community. please note: this is an unpaid program and is not an internship To be successful in this role you: Have experience in leveraging or critically thinking about how to integrate AI into work processes, decision-making, or problem-solving. This may include using AI-powered tools, automating workflows, analyzing AI-driven insights, or exploring AI’s potential impact on the function or industry . Are an Undergraduate student majoring or minoring in Computer Science (CS), Computer Engineering (CE), or Data Analytics. or related field, with a graduation date no earlier than December 2027 Are experienced in Python programming. Are experienced with and/or have knowledge of fundamental AI concepts Have availability to attend the full duration of the boot camp from June 15, 2026 to July 31, 2026 and then available to participate onsite in the beginning of August Application Process: Interested candidates should apply by April 15, 2026 , to be considered. Applications are evaluated until the application deadline only; therefore, early submission is recommended as spots are limited! Please submit a resume, a cover letter, and any related project work or AI experience. In your cover letter please share: Why do you want to participate in this AI bootcamp? Where do you see AI helping you in the future?

This is a remote position with up to 50% domestic travel required. Candidates may reside in the Southwest or Western part of the United States and should expect frequent national travel. The AbbVie Employer NAE is responsible for supporting and implementing strategic business initiatives in response to the changing healthcare environment, deployed specifically to national Employer Stakeholders via the AbbVie Employer Team with a focus on improving workforce health and productivity and maximizing strategic access to AbbVie’s therapies. The Employer NAE will be accountable for building effective stakeholder strategies and engagements that are on the forefront of emerging concerns impacting employee access, affordability, disease state awareness/management and medication value and access. This includes healthcare decision-makers (HCDMs) within national employer plan sponsors, employee benefit consultants (EBCs), and employer coalitions, as well as emerging stakeholders/influencers/vendors, national organizations, and professional/advocacy organizations. The Employer NAE provides branded and unbranded messaging to employers and employer influencers/KOLs regarding the value and differentiation of AbbVie therapies to accelerate access to treatment and the use of benefit plan designs to identify and minimize barriers to affordable and predictable Rx access. The NAE also delivers messaging relating to disease state and burden of illness to increase the awareness of treatment solutions and explore solutions and develop best practices/case studies. The Employer NAE will provide leadership to distinguish AbbVie in the employer channel, be a convener of stakeholders and regional/national KOLs and SMEs, and provide strategic insights internally in support of evolving business needs to ensure timely awareness of market changes and trends and inform internal business leads to ensure a rapid response to external disruptors and Rx management strategies which impact affordable access to AbbVie’s therapies. This role is highly collaborative and consultative and requires partnering and interfacing with numerous cross-functional teams (Market Access leadership, Payer Strategy and Cross Portfolio Strategy and Pipeline, Training, Market Analytics Business Insights, Business Evolution Strategy Development (BESD), Brand Sales/Marketing, Government Affairs and Policy, Corporate Strategy, US Medical Affairs/Value & Access and Medical Outcomes Science & Science Liaisons (MOSLs); Finance, Legal, Compliance, Communications/PR, Field Reimbursement Leadership, Brand Sales/Marketing teams and internal Centers of Excellence (CoE). The NAE must demonstrate the ability to anticipate and act proactively and effectively in uncertain situations. Additionally, the NAE requires significant collaboration with the Corporate Accounts KAM teams, providing timely insights regarding evolving contracting trends and evolving rebate models, educating client-facing teams, and providing updates regarding downstream employer clients and formulary initiatives. This position does not have direct reports but does require the ability to manage and lead without authority across cross-functional teams while also being able to work independently and productively. The Employer NAE is the lead for regional employer initiatives working in conjunction with the Regional Account Executive (RAE) teams and Regional Directors, as well as compliant collaboration with the Population Heath Account Executive (PHAE) team. This includes identifying opportunities and/or employer access issues and training/educating and executing on use of Employer Team resources and messaging to health plan, health system, PBM and employer customers. This role also is a key collaborator with other national field-based teams including the Field Reimbursement team, educating team members on market disruptors and problem-solving on employer-focused access issues. The Employer NAE serves as a key role in cataloguing key disruptors and potential patient disruption and analyzing potential financial (Gross to Net) impact, as well as working across internal stakeholders to develop and execute mitigation strategies. Major Duties and Responsibilities: Proactively engage with existing employer stakeholders and identify/influence emerging employer stakeholders across the US. Identify insights, positions and potential impact of new and emerging employer stakeholders and vendors. Build proactive share of voice with employer customers and influencers on Rx management topics. Support and contribute to internal Strategy Teams regarding emerging strategies and identification of external SMEs. Collaborate with Government Affairs/Policy/Strategy Directors to connect and convene with new and emerging stakeholders and advocates. Work in conjunction with Employer Team Director and Marketing Director (and collaboratively with Principal National MOSL, Employer Channel) relative to employer channel resource development and messaging. Develop and deliver stakeholder appropriate resources to support access for the expanding AbbVie portfolio (DSA decks, case studies, condensed employer value-prop decks, case studies and benefit plan design resources) Cultivate national employer KOLs and advocates to help shape external education and policy in collaboration with Government Affairs/Policy/Strategy teams. Monitor, inform and deliver market insights to internal business partners. Lead education initiatives in conjunction with Market Access Training on key trends impacting purchasers and AbbVie access/gross-to-net. Establish AbbVie as credible source for non-branded information and disseminate via industry meetings and electronic sites / social media (consistent with AbbVie Communications/PR guidelines). Support efforts to integrate Employer Strategy into AbbVie Business Planning process. Assist AbbVie Employer Corporate Account Team Leader with managing budget and execution of sponsorships and memberships, consistent with AbbVie Office of Ethics and Compliance (OEC) guidelines. Establish AbbVie as a national leader and key partner in the employer channel. Work with Big 3 PBM/GPO KAM teams and respective rebate analysts to ensure contract compliance. Quantify volume/sales associated with employer child accounts and access changes. Participate in internal task forces relating to member/patient access. Bachelor’s degree in Business, Life Sciences, or a related field required. Minimum of 5 years of Account Executive or Market Access experience within the healthcare industry; employee benefits consulting (EBC) experience and/or PBM experience is a plus. Proven ability to operate effectively in large, complex geographies, influence diverse stakeholders, and deliver commercial results. Demonstrated capability in negotiation, stakeholder engagement, and strategic planning/development and execution. Strong analytical skills, especially related to Rx contract terms/language and the commercial payor market. Effective communication and presentation skills (written and oral) with both technical and non-technical audiences. Experience managing complexity and collaborating with cross-functional, matrixed teams; agility and team-orientation required. Customer-centric approach and proven ability to act as primary point of contact for internal and external stakeholders. Ability to work autonomously, manage ambiguity, and identify/influence key customers. Understanding of the evolving healthcare environment—including ACA, CAA, ERISA, clinical guidelines, and formulary/utilization management. Adept at delivering product and disease state value proposition materials to a range of customers. Highest ethical standards and compliance with AbbVie Office of Ethics and Compliance (OEC) policies. The AbbVie Process Chemistry Chromatographic Separations Lab is actively seeking an Associate Scientist II or Scientist I. Our team collaborates with colleagues across multiple disciplines, offering expertise in preparative chromatography to support a broad range of AbbVie R&D programs. We maintain and utilize specialized equipment for various separation tasks, including the purification of peptides, ADC drug-linkers, and chiral compounds, as well as the isolation of low-level API impurities. Additionally, the team is responsible for pilot-scale preparative purification, developing scalable purification processes, and overseeing their implementation under cGMP guidelines at AbbVie's North Chicago Chemical Pilot Plant. This role will contribute to the development of novel/advanced separations technologies and broader efforts to develop new process technologies for advancing the AbbVie pipeline. We are seeking a motivated scientist who demonstrates initiative and technical proficiency in supporting research and development projects within a collaborative team environment. The ideal candidate will have hands-on experience developing chromatographic methods and troubleshooting complex separation challenges. Experience working with peptides is highly desirable, but not required for application. Key Responsibilities: Develop and execute purification processes supporting development of small molecule, antibody drug conjugate, and peptide clinical candidates. Demonstrate scientific initiative and creativity in planning, executing, and troubleshooting experiments, resolving key project challenges with an appropriate level of autonomy based on experience. Conduct a range of laboratory and pilot-scale tasks, analyze and interpret data, and drive project objectives, assuming responsibility for tasks in accordance with experience. Suggest, adapt, and, as appropriate, implement new or improved experimental protocols/techniques, consulting relevant literature as needed. We have an opening for a NEST Readiness Coordinator to oversee and execute LLNL’s Nuclear Emergency Support Team (NEST) responder readiness program. This role requires familiarity with DOE Order 153.1 and LLNL’s compliance with these requirements. You will administer and maintain readiness and training records, execute routine readiness checks and notifications using established procedures, and prepare recurring reports for program customers and management. Additional key aspects of the program include coordination of the on-call watchbill schedule, determining which qualified responders are assigned to on-call periods based on established eligibility and coverage requirements, and verifying required training and readiness items are current prior to assignment. The position coordinates updates across institutional systems and stakeholders, resolves routine issues by interpreting applicable guidelines, and escalates discrepancies that could impact readiness or on-call coverage. This position will be in the NEST Program Element within the Global Security Principal Directorate’s Nuclear Threat Reduction (N) Program. In this role, you will Participates in the development, maintenance, and improvement of the NEST responder readiness database and associated tools. Partner with the Readiness Program Lead, assess and analyze established readiness support processes and workflows, ensuring tasks are completed accurately and on time. Respond to customer questions and resolve routine readiness administration issues by interpreting and explaining procedures, guidelines, and manuals. Maintain, review data, and summarize results to support resolution of readiness discrepancies. Maintain service area records, databases, and documentation for responder readiness and training tracking. Collect, validate, reconcile, compile, and report readiness information across systems, such as, ARMS, TRAKEN, WCD, and related tools. Prepare routine and standard reports for customer use and management decision-making, including completion status, discrepancy tracking, and readiness summaries. Monitor routine readiness checks, notifications, and follow-ups; track completion and document exceptions. Maintain an escalation contact list/tree for routing readiness issues to the appropriate points of contact. Build, publish, and maintain the LLNL Master NEST on-call watch and deployment roster, determining on-call assignments using established coverage rules, qualification criteria, and availability inputs from Deployment POCs and responder organizations. Maintain documentation of responder requirements (on-call expectations, baseline training, gear and communications requirements as applicable), updating content per established guidance. Support upkeep of the NEST Deskbook by performing updates, maintaining version control, and routing edits for review/approval per defined process. Maintain a database used to document NEST facility capabilities, resources, and configurations. Coordinate onboarding/offboarding administrative steps for contractor and subcontractor personnel that support NEST readiness, such as, access requests, account tracking, required documentation, and following established procedures. Track issuance and inventory records for communications devices, such as,pagers, cell phones, Starlink units, and coordinate updates with supporting organizations. Support tracking of vendor/contract readiness-related information by maintaining records and reporting actions to the appropriate contract or technical points of contact. Perform other duties as assigned. This position requires an Active DOE Q clearance (or active Top-Secret clearance) with ability to obtain Sensitive Compartmented Information access. Experience coordinating responder readiness activities, workflow, and processes in- service operations, customer service, operations support, logistics, or mission support environment. Ability to maintain accurate records, databases, and documentation using tools such as SharePoint lists/libraries, spreadsheets, or similar systems. Experience in collecting, validating, and reporting operational data with attention to detail and data integrity. Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to document processes and requirements clearly and explain procedures to customers. Experience in tracking and coordinating multiple, parallel tasks and following through discrepancies to closure. Experience working collaboratively with cross-functional teams and multiple stakeholders. Must have a valid California driver’s license. Qualifications We Desire Bachelor’s degree in business, accounting, finance, information management/technology, or related field, or equivalent combination of education and related experience. Experience in technical operations, logistics, mission support, or emergency/incident response environments. Familiarity with LLNL and/or NEST-associated systems and processes, such as, ARMS, TRAKEN, WCD, paging/cell systems, or similar tracking and communication tools. Experience with reporting tools, such as, SharePoint and dashboards. Experience in preparing recurring operational status reports and creating basic graphical summaries, charts, and tables. Experience supporting and improving operational processes and documentation including standard operating processes, deskbooks, and playbooks; editing, version control, routing updates; consolidating requirements; and developing new tracking methods or tools. The Center for Global Security Research (CGSR) was established at Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL) in 1996 to bring together experts from the science, technology, and policy communities to address pressing national security challenges. For over 20 years, CGSR has engaged diverse perspectives on topics important to national security, deterrence, diplomacy, dual-use technology, arms control, nonproliferation, space, cyber, biosecurity, and energy security. We have openings in Fall 2026 for undergraduate students to engage in practical research on global security topics. Students will work with CGSR over the duration of three to four months as a research associate (RA). RAs will engage in practical research to further their educational and career goals, while also supporting the development of strategies for national security and LLNL’s mission focus areas. Examples of relevant fields of research include nuclear deterrence, arms control, nonproliferation, emerging technologies, cybersecurity, space, biological & chemical security, and energy security. CGSR’s objectives are as follows: To explore the dynamics of potential 21st century strategic conflicts (i.e., those with a potential nuclear aspect) and to formulate ideas about how to achieve U.S. deterrence and other objectives in such conflicts. To explore the sources and characteristics of strategic competition in the emerging security environment and to formulate organizing concepts to enhance the competitive position of the United States and its allies and partners over the long term. To identify whether and how technically based approaches can address new challenges to national and international security. To catalyze broader national and international thinking about the requirements of effective deterrence, assurance, and strategic stability in a changed and changing security environment. To assist in the development of new generations of experts motivated by a clear view of the changed and changing security environment. More information on CGSR, its research focus areas, and its publications can be found at https://cgsr.llnl.gov/ . This job will be closed to applicants on May 31, 2026. You will Conduct an independent research project on an agreed upon topic aligned with CGSR/LLNL research priorities under the supervision of CGSR staff. Support CGSR/LLNL through contributions to ongoing research activities. Tasks may include contributing to literature reviews, annotated bibliographies, and workshop summary reports. Attend relevant research seminars, speakers’ series, and workshops. Present research to LLNL staff at end of the assignment. Prepare end-of-assignment technical report or publication. Perform all assignments in accordance with ES&H, security, and business practice requirements and policies. Perform other duties as assigned. Must be eligible to access the Laboratory in compliance with Section 3112 of the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA). See Additional Information section below for details. Must be currently enrolled in an accredited university or have completed AA/AS degree in a field of research aligned with CGSR analytic priorities. Areas of study include international relations and/or security, political science, economics, public policy, emerging technologies, nonproliferation, energy, biosecurity, foreign language studies, or related fields. Demonstrated academic and/or professional achievement in a relevant field of research aligned with CGSR analytic priorities. Strong record of independent research and publication, or a strong proposal of research to be done while at CGSR and in future academic and professional settings. Ability to work in a team environment. Pay Range $23.26 - $31.62 Hourly This position is under a step structure. Please note that the step is determined by your academic level. Transcripts are required.

In this role you will: Conduct an independent research project on an agreed upon topic aligned with CGSR/LLNL research priorities. Effective interpersonal skills with the ability to work in a team environment. Pay Range $6,752 - $8,201 Monthly This position is under a step structure. Please note that the step placement is determined by your most recent completed academic year.

These positions are field based / remote in the following locations: CA, WA, OR, IA, MN, IN, OH, FL. Candidates must reside in one of the these states and be willing to travel for site visits. Purpose Advance AbbVie's pipeline by striving for excellence in clinical research, turning science into medicine for our patients and leveraging new advanced capabilities to drive industry leading performance. Partners with the investigator and site staff for meaningful and effective engagements positioning AbbVie as the choice in clinical trials. Focus on site clinical research that ensures appropriate conduct of the trial while driving improvement in data integrity, compliance, overall study performance and customer experience. Responsibilities Considered as the primary point of contact for the investigative site. High level of competency or experience in providing contextual information on the clinical trials, connects stakeholder to the investigative sites and strengthens AbbVie’s positioning. Aligns, trains and motivates the site staff and principal investigator on the goals of the clinical trial program, protocol and patient treatment principles for the trial ensuring a trusted partnership. Conducts site evaluation, site training, routine, and site closure monitoring activities with compliance to the protocol and monitoring plans, in accordance with applicable regulations, Good Clinical Practices (GCPs), ICH Guidelines, AbbVie Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), and quality standards, ensuring safety and protection of study subjects. Advanced understanding of site engagement and ability to customize site engagement strategy for assigned study (ies). Gather local/site insights and utilize site engagement tools such as the Customer Relationship Management (CRM) tool, to report/track progress and measure impact of that strategy. Advanced level of competency connecting the study protocol, scientific principles and clinical trial requirements to the day-to-day clinical trial execution activities. Evaluate and ensure effective recruitment and retention techniques/plans based on the patient disease journey. Develop solid knowledge of therapeutic area, asset and clinical landscape / patient journey to enable successful patient recruitment and overall protocol compliance. Possesses experienced level of competency to mentor and train less experienced CRAs on various aspects of work and provides input into their development. May participate in global/local task forces and initiatives. Responsible for activities as assigned by manager. Responsible for continuous risk-assessment proactively, and in collaboration with Central Monitoring team, monitor activities conducted by clinical sites to detect early overall study performance or patient safety issues. Advanced ability to think critically to resolve site risk signals while having robust understanding of site processes to drive study execution. Ensures preventative and corrective action plans are put into place, as needed, to mitigate risk and promote compliance using a customer centric approach. Identifies, evaluates and recommends new/potential investigators/sites on an on going basis. Potential sites may be identified through networking or internal AbbVie requests to assist in the placement of planned clinical studies with qualified investigators. Ensures quality of data submitted from study sites and assures timely submission of data, including appropriate reporting and follow-up for all safety events by site personnel. Ensures audit and regulatory inspection readiness at assigned clinical site at all times. Manages investigator payments as per executed contract obligations, as applicable. Minimum of 1 year of clinically related experience, of which a period of 6 months is required in clinical research monitoring of investigational drug or device trials. Familiar with risk‐based monitoring approach, onsite and offsite monitoring. Knowledge of appropriate therapeutic area indications is preferred with the ability to understand and apply scientific concepts as they relate to the conduct of clinical trials. Advanced knowledge on existing and emerging local regulatory and legal requirements, ICH/GCP Guidelines and applicable policies. Demonstrate strong cross-functional collaboration skills among internal and external stakeholders. Demonstrate strong planning and organizational skills and the ability to work effectively and efficiently in a dynamic environment with competing projects and deadlines. Advanced ability to leverage technology, tools and resources to provide customer centric support based on the health of the site. Strong interpersonal skills with excellent written, verbal, active listening and presentation skills, with ability to establish and leverage site relationships and trusted partnerships through engagement, motivation, and training. Ability to use functional expertise with appropriate guidance, leverage critical thinking skills and apply good judgement to address clinical site issues. Acts with integrity in accordance with AbbVie code of business conduct and leadership values. Self-motivated individual focused on delivering timely and quality outcomes in a fast-paced environment.

We have an opening for a Cloud Operations Engineer to join our team. In this position, you will be responsible for designing, implementing, and managing cloud solutions that support the National Nuclear Security Administration’s (NNSA) business services and programmatic missions, including scientific research and mission-critical operations. This position is in the Enterprise Infrastructure Services (EIS) Division within the Computing Directorate. You will work closely with multidisciplinary teams to drive innovation, improve scalability, and ensure the secure and efficient utilization of cloud resources for NNSA initiatives. This role supports multiple sites across the country and occasional travel is required to collaborate with stakeholders and partners. This position offers the opportunity to work in a dynamic and highly technical environment, supporting critical infrastructure for enterprise-level applications. This position requires full-time on-site presence due to the nature of the work. This position will be filled at either the SES.2 or SES.3 level based on knowledge and related experience as assessed by the hiring team. Additional job responsibilities (outlined below) will be assigned if hired at the higher level. In this role you will Deploy and manage cloud infrastructure (primarily AWS) in support of scientific, engineering, and business applications. Develop automation scripts and Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) solutions for cloud resource provisioning and management. Collaborate with researchers, engineers, and IT staff to migrate workloads and optimize applications for cloud environments. Implement and manage cloud financial operations (FinOps) practices to optimize cloud spending, track usage, and collaborate with stakeholders to ensure cost-effective resource allocation. Monitor cloud performance and usage, and implement solutions for high availability, scalability, and cost efficiency. Ensure compliance with Department of Energy (DOE) and NNSA security policies and federal regulations for cloud operations. Provide technical support, documentation, and training for cloud users across the enterprise. Stay abreast of emerging cloud technologies and recommend adoption of innovative solutions. Perform other duties as assigned. Additional job responsibilities at the SES.3 Level Develop and implement advanced cloud computing environments that align with customer needs and enterprise system strategies, ensuring optimal performance and scalability. Independently configure and utilize systems and cloud management tools to monitor, maintain, and optimize infrastructure operations effectively. Identify, troubleshoot, and document complex system and network issues to ensure timely resolution and minimize disruptions. Ability to obtain and maintain a US DOE Q-level security clearance which requires U.S. Citizenship. Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of technical education and relevant experience. Broad experience in cloud platform administration and support, with proficiency in technologies such as AWS, Azure, Google Cloud Platform, or hybrid cloud environments. Broad knowledge of cloud infrastructure operations, including resource provisioning, automation, and the use of infrastructure management tools. Proficient understanding of cloud support systems, such as virtual networking, identity and access management, and monitoring solutions. Comprehensive experience with cloud architecture documentation tools, including Visio and other office productivity software. Proficient in managing and troubleshooting cloud-based resources and services, including performance monitoring and incident response. Strong interpersonal, verbal, and written communication skills, with the ability to work independently while effectively collaborating with customers and team members. Additional Qualifications at the SES.3 Level Significant experience managing enterprise cloud environments, including platforms such as AWS, Azure, and hybrid cloud networking. Advanced knowledge of troubleshooting techniques, with strong skills in resolving issues through analysis of logs, metrics, and cloud-native diagnostic tools. Significant experience with resource provisioning, automation, and infrastructure as management tools, such as Terraform, CloudFormation, Cloud Development Kit, or similar platforms. Significant experience training and mentoring team members, focusing on cloud engineering best practices and architectural design principles. Desired Qualifications Active Department of Energy (DOE) Q-level clearance or active Top-Secret clearance issued by another U.S. government agency at the time of hire. AWS Certified Solutions Architect credential or an equivalent advanced cloud certification. Deep familiarity with hybrid cloud architectures and expert-level proficiency in integrating on-premises environments with cloud platforms in air-gapped environments. Comprehensive knowledge of compliance frameworks, such as National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), FedRAMP, and related standards, with proven experience implementing and maintaining compliance within cloud environments. This is a remote position with up to 50% domestic travel required. Candidates may reside in any state within the United States and should expect frequent national travel. The AbbVie Employer NAE is responsible for supporting and implementing strategic business initiatives in response to the changing healthcare environment, deployed specifically to national Employer Stakeholders via the AbbVie Employer Team with a focus on improving workforce health and productivity and maximizing strategic access to AbbVie’s therapies. The Employer NAE will be accountable for building effective stakeholder strategies and engagements that are on the forefront of emerging concerns impacting employee access, affordability, disease state awareness/management and medication value and access. This includes healthcare decision-makers (HCDMs) within national employer plan sponsors, employee benefit consultants (EBCs), and employer coalitions, as well as emerging stakeholders/influencers/vendors, national organizations, and professional/advocacy organizations. The Employer NAE provides branded and unbranded messaging to employers and employer influencers/KOLs regarding the value and differentiation of AbbVie therapies to accelerate access to treatment and the use of benefit plan designs to identify and minimize barriers to affordable and predictable Rx access. The NAE also delivers messaging relating to disease state and burden of illness to increase the awareness of treatment solutions and explore solutions and develop best practices/case studies. The Employer NAE will provide leadership to distinguish AbbVie in the employer channel, be a convener of stakeholders and regional/national KOLs and SMEs, and provide strategic insights internally in support of evolving business needs to ensure timely awareness of market changes and trends and inform internal business leads to ensure a rapid response to external disruptors and Rx management strategies which impact affordable access to AbbVie’s therapies. This role is highly collaborative and consultative and requires partnering and interfacing with numerous cross-functional teams (Market Access leadership, Payer Strategy and Cross Portfolio Strategy and Pipeline, Training, Market Analytics Business Insights, Business Evolution Strategy Development (BESD), Brand Sales/Marketing, Government Affairs and Policy, Corporate Strategy, US Medical Affairs/Value & Access and Medical Outcomes Science & Science Liaisons (MOSLs); Finance, Legal, Compliance, Communications/PR, Field Reimbursement Leadership, Brand Sales/Marketing teams and internal Centers of Excellence (CoE). The NAE must demonstrate the ability to anticipate and act proactively and effectively in uncertain situations. Additionally, the NAE requires significant collaboration with the Corporate Accounts KAM teams, providing timely insights regarding evolving contracting trends and evolving rebate models, educating client-facing teams, and providing updates regarding downstream employer clients and formulary initiatives. This position does not have direct reports but does require the ability to manage and lead without authority across cross-functional teams while also being able to work independently and productively. The Employer NAE is the lead for regional employer initiatives working in conjunction with the Regional Account Executive (RAE) teams and Regional Directors, as well as compliant collaboration with the Population Heath Account Executive (PHAE) team. This includes identifying opportunities and/or employer access issues and training/educating and executing on use of Employer Team resources and messaging to health plan, health system, PBM and employer customers. This role also is a key collaborator with other national field-based teams including the Field Reimbursement team, educating team members on market disruptors and problem-solving on employer-focused access issues. The Employer NAE serves as a key role in cataloguing key disruptors and potential patient disruption and analyzing potential financial (Gross to Net) impact, as well as working across internal stakeholders to develop and execute mitigation strategies. Major Duties and Responsibilities: Proactively engage with existing employer stakeholders and identify/influence emerging employer stakeholders across the US. Identify insights, positions and potential impact of new and emerging employer stakeholders and vendors. Build proactive share of voice with employer customers and influencers on Rx management topics. Support and contribute to internal Strategy Teams regarding emerging strategies and identification of external SMEs. Collaborate with Government Affairs/Policy/Strategy Directors to connect and convene with new and emerging stakeholders and advocates. Work in conjunction with Employer Team Director and Marketing Director (and collaboratively with Principal National MOSL, Employer Channel) relative to employer channel resource development and messaging. Develop and deliver stakeholder appropriate resources to support access for the expanding AbbVie portfolio (DSA decks, case studies, condensed employer value-prop decks, case studies and benefit plan design resources) Cultivate national employer KOLs and advocates to help shape external education and policy in collaboration with Government Affairs/Policy/Strategy teams. Monitor, inform and deliver market insights to internal business partners. Lead education initiatives in conjunction with Market Access Training on key trends impacting purchasers and AbbVie access/gross-to-net. Establish AbbVie as credible source for non-branded information and disseminate via industry meetings and electronic sites / social media (consistent with AbbVie Communications/PR guidelines). Support efforts to integrate Employer Strategy into AbbVie Business Planning process. Assist AbbVie Employer Corporate Account Team Leader with managing budget and execution of sponsorships and memberships, consistent with AbbVie Office of Ethics and Compliance (OEC) guidelines. Establish AbbVie as a national leader and key partner in the employer channel. Work with Big 3 PBM/GPO KAM teams and respective rebate analysts to ensure contract compliance. Quantify volume/sales associated with employer child accounts and access changes. Participate in internal task forces relating to member/patient access. Bachelor’s degree in Business, Life Sciences, or a related field required. Minimum of 5 years of Account Executive or Market Access experience within the healthcare industry; employee benefits consulting (EBC) experience and/or PBM experience is a plus. Proven ability to operate effectively in large, complex geographies, influence diverse stakeholders, and deliver commercial results. Demonstrated capability in negotiation, stakeholder engagement, and strategic planning/development and execution. Strong analytical skills, especially related to Rx contract terms/language and the commercial payor market. Effective communication and presentation skills (written and oral) with both technical and non-technical audiences. Experience managing complexity and collaborating with cross-functional, matrixed teams; agility and team-orientation required. Customer-centric approach and proven ability to act as primary point of contact for internal and external stakeholders. Ability to work autonomously, manage ambiguity, and identify/influence key customers. Understanding of the evolving healthcare environment—including ACA, CAA, ERISA, clinical guidelines, and formulary/utilization management. Adept at delivering product and disease state value proposition materials to a range of customers. Highest ethical standards and compliance with AbbVie Office of Ethics and Compliance (OEC) policies. Significant domestic travel required (up to 50%) for customer interactions, industry meetings and internal meetings. An essential requirement of your position is to satisfy all applicable health care industry representative (HCIR) credentialing requirements to gain and maintain entry into facilities and organizations that are in your assigned territory. You must also be in good standing and/or eligible to obtain these credentials. Driving a personal auto or company car or truck, or a powered piece of material handling equipment. Valid driver’s license: Ability to pass a pre-employment drug screening test and meet safe driving requirements. Preferred: 10+ years’ experience in pharmaceutical, Rx supply chain, employee benefit consulting, or healthcare organization. Deep understanding of commercial business models and payor markets.

Position Summary Machine/grind parts/tools to conform to blueprints/drawings Duties and responsibilities The following reflects management’s definition of essential functions for this job but does not restrict the tasks that may be assigned. Management may assign or reassign duties and responsibilities to this job at any time due to reasonable accommodation or other reasons Maintain accurate inventory levels of CNC and HMC tooling, ensuring proper organization and storage. We have an opening for a Software Engineer to support the Collaborative Authorization for the Safety-basis Total Lifecycle Environment (CASTLE-PX) Project. CASTLE-PX is Risk Level 2 Safety Software, requiring a high-level of rigor to maintain SQA compliance. CASTLE-PX is a web-based, custom Java application deployed at Pantex and is being used to manage the safety-bases for weapon systems, site facilities, as well as several business processes. Working with a dynamic multi-disciplinary team of software developers, software quality engineers, and IT staff, your primary responsibilities will be to contribute to the application development, perform production support, test new releases, and help maintain the large volume of SQA support documents. This position is in the Applications, Simulations, and Quality (ASQ) Division within the Computing Directorate, in support of the CASTLE Project within the Weapon Technologies Engineering (WTE) Program. This position offers a hybrid schedule, blending in-person and virtual presence. You may have the flexibility to work from home a maximum of 2 days per week. We have an opening for a Field Technician to provide technical support and customer services in the management of hazardous and radioactive waste. Under general supervision you will perform a variety of technical functions in collecting, packaging, labeling, identifying, documenting, segregating, consolidating, treating, and storing hazardous, explosive and radioactive waste generated by various LLNL programs. This position is in the Radioactive and Hazardous Waste Management (RHWM) Program and part of the Special Project Group supporting Site 200 within the Strategic Deterrence Directorate. This position requires full-time on-site presence due to the nature of the work. This position will be filled at either level based on knowledge and related experience as assessed by the hiring team. Additional job responsibilities (outlined below) will be assigned if hired at the higher level. In this role you will Perform a wide variety of waste management activities, often wearing personal protective equipment (PPE) such as anti-C’s, respirator, hearing protection, etc., to collect, package, label, identify, segregate, consolidate, treat, store, and verify hazardous, low level radioactive, mixed and/or transuranic waste. Operate wastewater retention tanks and/or systems, perform pump-outs, perform lab packing of waste chemicals and manage waste container storage areas. Perform field testing (pH, visual etc.) and sampling of waste to verify characterization and/or treatment results and operate radiation survey instruments to obtain radiological data. Operate a variety of vehicles up to and including 5-ton trucks, use material handling equipment (fork trucks, drum handling equipment, mechanical pump systems, etc.), and use hand and power tools. Respond to environmental emergencies at LLNL and work with cross-organizational personnel performing decontamination of facility infrastructure and equipment. Gather, analyze, and record basic pertinent data and maintain detailed and accurate records associated with radioactive and hazardous waste to properly characterize and manage the waste. Complete and maintain training requirements per Federal, State, and LLNL requirements. Provide high-end customer service with a wide range of waste generators as the front-line interface between RHWM and waste generators. Support various scope Decontamination and Demolition (D&D) projects on behalf of LLNL. Perform all assignments in accordance with ES&H, security, and business practice requirements and policies. Perform other duties as assigned. Additional job responsibilities at the 504.3 Level Solve difficult radioactive and hazardous waste management problems using established guidelines and routine techniques and procedures. Plan and execute waste management projects including directing the activities of other technicians. Conduct On-the-Job-Training and provide mentoring and leadership for less experienced technicians. Act as Responsible Individual (RI) on Work Control Documents. Ability to secure and maintain a U.S. DOE Q-level security clearance which requires U.S. citizenship. Associate degree in environmental or related scientific field, or equivalent combination of education and experience. Intermediate knowledge of State and Federal regulations as they apply to hazardous and radioactive waste management, with emphasis on managing waste in satellite accumulation areas (SAAs) and 90-day consolidated accumulation areas (CAAs) or experience working within nuclear or high-hazard facilities. Intermediate knowledge of field instrumentation, such as radiation survey instruments, pH meters, etc., with an emphasis on their application to radioactive and hazardous waste processes. Elementary understanding of chemistry principles, including compatibility, and/or general understanding of radioactive contamination control methods. Ability to meet medical qualification to wear respiratory protection equipment, climb ladders and meet other physical requirements specified in the job demands worksheet and to successfully complete all Federal, State, LLNL and Department of Transportation (DOT) training requirements. Effective communication and interpersonal skills in order to build and maintain working relationships with coworkers, waste generators, programmatic support personnel and management. Strong organizational skills with the ability to generate and maintain high-quality, accurate records and correspondence using PC and/or Apple workstations and associated applications. Effective customer service skills needed to provide waste management support to a wide range of waste generators. Additional qualifications at the 504.3 Level Experience managing projects with minimal direction needed. High level understanding and knowledge of State and Federal regulations (RCRA, DOE, DOT) applicable to waste management, with demonstrated experience in their application or extensive experience working within nuclear facilities with a proven track record of accomplishing tasks while following strict controls. Experience with contaminated facility D&D. Experience providing training and mentoring to less experienced personnel. Pay Range $43.55 - $63.97 Hourly $43.55 - $53.36 Hourly for the 504.2 level $52.23 - $63.97 Hourly for the 504.3 level This is the lowest to highest salary we in good faith believe we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. An employee’s position within the salary range will be based on several factors including, but not limited to, specific competencies, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, seniority, geographic location, performance, and business or organizational needs.

We have an opening for a Document Compliance Coordinator to navigate a complex matrix of federal, institutional and organizational requirements. You will collaborate with engineers and subject matter experts to initiate, develop, document and evaluate comprehensive technical procedures, documents and safety plans. This position will support the Superblock (SBK) facility within the Strategic Deterrence Directorate. This position may offer a hybrid schedule, which includes the flexibility to work from home one or more days per week, after a probationary period. The specifics of the hybrid schedule, including the exact number of days required in the office and virtual work options, may vary based on the needs of the team and the organization. Additional job responsibilities (outlined below) will be assigned if hired at the higher level. In this role you will Analyze and implement documentation processes, procedures, and practices to ensure activities within the facility are performed in compliance with requirements in federal regulations, institutional procedures, and the nuclear facility safety bases. Evaluate procedures and process documents to verify facility requirements are adequately implemented, controls identified in the safety basis documents are maintained, and technical and management reviews are conducted. Serve as a contact for SBK processes, procedures, practices, manuals, guidance documents and safety plans and provide guidance to others related to SBK administrative procedures associated with document compliance. Collaborate with subject matter experts to initiate, develop, review, revise, implement and evaluate documentation that impact SBK facilities and systems, as well as LLNL programs. Assist in planning, coordinating, and conducting periodic assessments to determine conformance with regulations, LLNL requirements, and SBK plans and procedures, including management self-assessments, observations and inspections, relating to SBK processes and other operational activities; recommend and coordinate completion of corrective action plans related to deficiencies. Manage technical information communications and interface with the LLNL programs and facilities personnel related to facility procedures; solicit feedback and facilitate comment resolution. Perform other duties as assigned. Additional job responsibilities, at the A23.3 level Develop, plan, review, assess, analyze, and implement administrative processes, procedures, and practices by applying in depth knowledge to ensure SBK activities comply with governing requirements, including federal regulations, LLNL procedures, and nuclear facility safety basis documents. Provide professional support to program/practice/policy development and implementation efforts; assists with program research and ongoing monitoring of results. Serves as a subject matter expert and trusted resource, providing informed recommendations to management on policy updates and changes. Ability to secure and maintain a U.S. DOE Q level security clearance which requires U.S. citizenship. Associate Degree in a related field or equivalent combination of education and related experience in a business, operational and/or organizational area. Experience interpreting, reviewing and analyzing administrative processes, policies, procedures and practices to determine if the activities they address are performed in compliance with complex regulations and requirements. Effective technical composition, writing and editing skills and experience effectively composing professional documentation with the ability to obtain a Procedure Professionals Association (PPA) Certification. Experience tracking, compiling and monitoring data necessary to coordinate corrective actions. Proficient verbal and written communication skills necessary to manage scientific and technical communications across multidisciplinary teams, with effective collaboration and communication skills necessary to effectively explain and present proposed changes to documents and processes. Effective organizational and interpersonal skills necessary to resolve problems and sensitive/confidential issues with tact, discretion, and mature judgment. Strong proficiency in Microsoft Word and a solid working knowledge of Excel, FileMaker Pro, Adobe Acrobat, and EDMS (such as SharePoint or Windchill) with the ability to learn new software quickly. Additional qualifications at the A23.3 level Experience researching, tracking, compiling and monitoring data necessary to conduct self-assessment activities, effectively present findings, and coordinate corrective actions. Broad and specialized knowledge of and experience in related work activities and multi-faceted internal processes. Experience training and mentoring personnel on document control within a regulated environment, ensuring compliance with applicable requirements. We are looking for a Counterintelligence Officer in the Counterintelligence Program to perform comprehensive research and analysis, conduct interviews, and present recommendations to senior management, high-level DOE personnel, and officials of intelligence agencies on relevant counterintelligence (CI) issues, ensuring the Laboratory’s compliance with Department of Energy (DOE) Order 475.1 (CI Program). Bachelor’s Degree in a related field or equivalent combination of education and related experience. Knowledge and experience working on national security issues related to the USIC. Broad knowledge of, and significant experience with, classified and unclassified databases, software applications, and other intelligence research tools to identify and assess foreign capabilities using the conventional intelligence disciplines. Specialized training and/or subject matter expertise, such as: counterespionage, interviewing, counterproliferation, weapons systems, and/or foreign intelligence services. You will be responsible for contributing to all-hazards emergency planning and preparedness programs in accordance with DOE and Laboratory requirements. You will also support operational response activities as a member of the Emergency Response Organization. This position is in the Planning and Preparedness Division, Emergency Management Department. Integrate technical analyses, including EPHA facility data, into emergency planning documents to ensure accurate hazard assessment and response strategies. Develop and refine Emergency Operations Center (EOC) processes for information management, decision support, and coordination with LLNL leadership and external agencies. Coordinate with Laboratory programs, facility management, and support organizations to ensure emergency plans are accurate, integrated, and executable. Serve as a member of the Emergency Response Organization, including qualification and participation in the Emergency Management Duty Officer (EMDO) off-hour duty rotation. Perform other duties as assigned. Perform computer modeling of hazardous material releases and consequence analyses to inform and scale emergency response capabilities. Develop technical reports and procedures and maintain Emergency Planning Hazards Assessments (EPHAs) for LLNL facilities with significant hazardous materials, applying rigorous hazards analysis methodologies. Develop and maintain Emergency Action Levels (EALs) to support rapid categorization and classification of Operational Emergencies. Ability to secure and maintain a U.S. DOE Q-level security clearance which requires U.S. citizenship. Bachelor’s degree in Emergency Management or related discipline, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience in emergency management response and/or working in, or managing, an emergency management, site, or security operations center. Demonstrated ability to independently develop and implement moderately complex emergency management solutions using established DOE and Laboratory standards. Comprehensive working knowledge of DOE Order 151.1 and Emergency Action Level (EAL) development methodologies for Operational Emergency classification. Ability to analyze technical hazard information (e.g., EPHA data) and integrate findings into practical, executable emergency planning documentation. Proficiency in applying established emergency management principles to improve Emergency Operations Center (EOC) processes and decision-support frameworks. Demonstrated capability to coordinate across organizational boundaries to ensure alignment of emergency planning with programmatic, facility, and operational requirements. Working knowledge of national emergency management standards sufficient to support compliance documentation and readiness assessments. Ability to evaluate lessons learned from exercises and incidents and recommend process improvements within established policy frameworks. Proven capability to exercise sound independent judgment during emergency response operations, including participation in duty officer rotations and Emergency Response Organization activities. Additional qualifications at the TSS.3 level Advanced knowledge in hazardous facility analysis and demonstrated ability to independently analyze complex, not well-defined technical problems and develop defensible, data-driven solutions using sound judgment and creativity within established Laboratory and regulatory frameworks. Proven ability to independently develop and maintain Emergency Planning Hazards Assessments (EPHAs), technical reports, and procedures for facilities with significant hazardous materials, applying advanced hazard analysis methodologies and exercising independent judgment in defining objectives and methods. Experience developing and maintaining Emergency Action Levels (EALs), applying advanced technical knowledge and independent judgment to ensure accurate categorization and classification of Operational Emergencies with programmatic and organizational impact. Working knowledge of DOE/NNSA regulatory requirements. Position Purpose: Provides day-to-day monitoring and basic plant and pump/booster station operations, routine lab tests and basic corrective and preventative maintenance activities. Primary Duties/Responsibilities: Operates equipment manually and through instrumentation panels, computer terminals and programmable logic control units following process control procedures. Monitors and observes operating conditions, records observations and data in shift log. Diagnoses basic operational problems and takes corrective action per procedure. Performs routine CLAIR (cleaning, lubrication, adjustment, inspection and minor repair) on machines and related equipment which may include pumps, engines, centrifuges, generators, valves, gates, mixers, conveyors, blowers, dryers, chemical feed, odor control, disinfection equipment, vacuum filters and belt presses. Reports and documents results of work performed and enters into appropriate database. Promptly reports any operational problems with machines or equipment to Lead or Supervisor. Collects water, wastewater, industrial waste, groundwater, sludge, residuals and/or gas samples according to schedule. Performs field tests (chemical, physical and biological) in order to pace chemical dosages for process and odor control units. Prepares chemical solutions, monitors supplies and recommends reorder. Performs routine lab tests and prepares reports per procedure. Performs routine instrument calibration for portable meters including, but not limited to, dissolved oxygen, pH, H2S, percent oxygen, lower explosive limit. Learns to inspect and becomes proficient at mechanical troubleshooting to determine repairs needed. Dismantles equipment to gain access to and repairs defective parts using hand tools, power tools and precision measuring and testing devices. Re-assembles and tests equipment ensuring safe and efficient operating condition is restored. Learns to troubleshoot hydraulic, pneumatic and electronic equipment and instrumentation. Performs manual labor including cleaning equipment, facilities and grounds as required and properly disposes of waste according to safety and environmental policies. Operates vehicles, mobile equipment and material handling equipment for operational and maintenance purposes. Performs facility maintenance and repair and may replace or install light bulbs, fluorescent tubes, damaged glass, windows, doors, partitions, ceiling or floor tiles, door locks, carpet, and/or paint. Learns to estimate time and material costs for various projects. May assist in other areas of facility as directed. Work Environment: Spends 100% of the time in operations environment. Typically spends 25 – 35% of time exposed to outdoor and sometimes inclement weather. Company service vehicles are used as required. Travels 1 – 2 times per year for company provided training. May be required to travel up to five consecutive days. May serve rotational 24 hour emergency on-call. Possible Work Hazards : May be exposed to possible operations hazards including fumes, dust, toxic and caustic chemicals, noise, rotating machinery, high pressure and hot and cold temperatures, slippery surfaces, water and electrical hazards. Education/Experience/Background: High school or GED with the ability to read, write and comprehend English (operational, process, safety and quality instructions) and be able to carry out verbal and written instructions. Six months to two years of experience in a related position with experience in a similar environment preferred with ability to comprehend specifications, blueprints and manuals. Experience using material handling equipment, pressure gauges and precision measuring instruments. Experience using power, pneumatic, hydraulic and hand tools and shop tools such as drill press, band saw, bench grinder, torque wrench preferred. Knowledge/Skills/Abilities: Ability to perform basic mathematical calculations. Some vocational training and mechanical aptitude preferred, with the ability to read, interpret and record data from meters, gauges, scales, panels, computer consoles and other equipment. Must have the ability to diagnose basic and routine process and mechanical problems and take remedial corrective action. Must have basic computer skills and have ability to operate programs for process control, the Computer Maintenance Management System, and laboratory/industrial pretreatment QA/QC. Must consistently demonstrate the ability to learn and independently perform assigned duties and meet or exceed production and quality goals. Must demonstrate ability to work in a team environment and willingness to assume additional or new responsibilities readily. Must be able to serve rotational 24-hour emergency on-call if required by site. Required Certification/Licenses/Training: Minimum water/wastewater license as required by regulatory agency at site. HAZWOPER (Hazardous Waste Operations and Emergency Response) Level I and II First Responder Certification if required by site. Obtain and maintain minimum water / wastewater operator state certification. Must become proficient in the care and use of all site specific, facility required PPE (Personal Protection Equipment), including respirators, gas detectors, confined space equipment, etc.) Forklift Certification if required by site. Training in operation of mechanical drives, hydraulic pumps and valves, pneumatics, electronics and control systems. Obtain HVAC, Electrician, Plumber’s or other trade License if assigned to that area. Note : Tech will not perform duties unless properly licensed. Training in the use of energy management systems as needed. Works toward increasing skills in additional functional areas or in obtaining advanced skills / maintenance certifications. Requires close visual and hearing observation to detect non-conformance and machine malfunction. Constantly uses hands to finger, handle or feel and frequently reaches with hands and arms. Works in various positions; works on ladders, catwalks, and supports at heights of 50 feet above the ground; and works with hands extended above and below head and body up to 40 minutes using hand tools weighing up to 15 pounds. We are seeking an experienced Cloud FinOps Analyst to join our dynamic team. You will be responsible for leading and implementing cloud & AI cost management and optimization strategies. Your primary focus will be on ensuring efficient cloud resource utilization, cost tracking, and identifying opportunities for cost savings within our cloud infrastructure, measuring & understanding AI usage across the organization. The Cloud FinOps analyst will be leading the cloud cost management across 10 different entities (including Visa) and any additional M&A entities. You will have knowledge of multiple cloud service providers (AWS, GCP, Azure, Oracle Cloud, AI tools and LLM providers etc.) and work with various technology teams to monitor and optimize resources on each platform. Responsibilities: Cost Analysis: Analyze cloud usage and cost trends, identify cost drivers, and provide actionable recommendations for cost optimization. Optimization strategies: Develop and implement strategies for optimizing cloud resources, including right-sizing of compute, storage, database, and other services, utilizing cost-effective services. Budget Management: Work closely with project teams to establish and manage cloud budgets, ensuring alignment with organization OKRs, implement effective cost management and optimization strategies. Develop and maintain financial models for cloud cost allocation. Set and Track budgets as per business unit requirements (by Account, by Project, by cost centers etc.). Forecasting: Collaborate with stakeholders to forecast future cloud & AI usage and costs for existing workloads and new projects/applications which can be moved from on-premises datacenters to cloud, providing insights in budget planning and resource allocation. Policy Development: Establish and enforce cloud & AI cost management policies, guidelines, and best practices across organization. Continuous monitoring: Implement monitoring mechanisms to track cloud & AI costs in real time and proactively address anomalies and deviations from budgetary expectations. Reporting: Generate regular reports and dashboards to communicate cost-related insights, trends, and recommendations to management and relevant stakeholders. Stay updated: Keep abreast of industry trends, new cloud services, and pricing models to ensure the organization remains cost effective and competitive. This is a hybrid position. Expectation of days in office will be confirmed by your hiring manager. Basic Qualifications: 2+ years of relevant work experience and a Bachelors degree, OR 5+ years of relevant work experience Preferred Qualifications: 3 or more years of work experience with a Bachelor’s Degree or more than 2 years of work experience with an Advanced Degree (e.g. Masters, MBA, JD, MD) Master’s degree or Bachelor’s degree in Management Information Systems, Computer Science, Finance, or related field. 4+ years of experience in financial analysis, preferably in a technology or cloud computing environment. Proven experience in cloud cost management and optimization with a minimum of 4 years in a similar role. Strong understanding of cloud pricing, cost structures, and billing models. Proficient in cloud platforms like AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud. Excellent analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making skills. Strong communication skills to effectively collaborate with cross-functional teams. Proficiency in data analysis tools and software. Certification in Cloud FinOps or related field. Experience with cloud cost management tools. Advanced proficiency in Excel, Powerpoint and other Microsoft Office applications.
